one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban analyzes three Sandiganbayan Second Division resolutions (Sandoval, chair; Diaz-Baldos and Martires, members) on the Garcia plea bargain agreement. Martires's 157-page resolution (May 9) denied OSG intervention for 'utter paucity of merit,' finding that the prosecution filed a 'defectively worded information' and 'miserably failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond reasonable doubt.' Baldos's 22-page resolution (May 9) approved the PBA, which convicted Garcia of direct bribery and facilitating money laundering and recovered P135 million. Sandoval's 3-page resolution (May 6) denied the inhibition motion. The author notes that Martires devoted over 100 pages scrutinizing testimonial and documentary evidence before his conclusion -- and that SBN justices' factual findings carry great persuasive value because they observed witness demeanor firsthand. To overturn them, the OSG would need to show grave factual error. Though the author cannot evaluate the SBN's findings without record access, he observes that Garcia's defense counsel (Constantino de Jesus) must have studied the evidence and concluded the PBA was in Garcia's best interest -- otherwise, a demurrer would have been the free and safer option, suggesting the evidence was actually sufficient to convict for plunder.
